turns.user: People sometimes get two invitation emails when they double-click Invite. Should we debounce the button or fix this on the server?
turns.observations: The frontend sends POST /invites on each click. The server creates an invite and sends an email for each request. There is no request deduplication. Clients may also retry requests after timeouts.

turns.user: Okay, go with the server fix and disable the button while it's sending. Where are we at?
turns.observations: Work performed: the client reuses an idempotency key for retries of the same submission and disables Invite while the request is pending. The server uses a database unique constraint on the idempotency key to claim the request before enqueueing email. The simultaneous-request test passes with one email queued. Still unchecked: behavior when the email provider rejects the queued send.

turns.user: Hang on, I still need to resend an invite if someone loses the email. Does your fix stop that?
turns.observations: A deliberate resend creates a new idempotency key. Retries of the same submission reuse its existing key. The database does not enforce uniqueness on the recipient email. The resend path has not yet been tested.

turns.user: Cool. Test that and the failure case, then give me the handoff.
